title: I Used the Airline Seat-Swap Screenshot as the Whole Complaint

parts.text: I boarded at 6:08 a.m. with a window I had paid fourteen extra dollars to pick. A man in a quarter-zip was already in 14A, holding a paper cup that smelled like gate-coffee and mint gum. "My wife needs the window," he said. "She's anxious." His wife was in 14B looking at her phone, not anxious, booking a lounge. I was thirty-six, flying for a funeral, holding a boarding pass that still had WINDOW printed. The flight attendant asked if I would be a hero. I said I would be a screenshot. I photographed my seat map, the extra-fee line, and his boarding pass which showed 14C. He had moved himself. The plane door was still open. He told me I was making a scene. I forwarded the photos to the airline chat before we pushed. Then the app pinged: SEAT CHANGE PENDING — 14A TO 31E. Someone in the back office was "helping."
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The app is trying to move me to 31E while the door is still open and my paid window is occupied.

social.video_title: He sat in my paid window and called it anxiety — Part 1/2
social.description: Fourteen dollars, a quarter-zip in 14A, and an app that tried to "help" me to the back. Would you have stood in the aisle?

parts.text: I showed the flight attendant the pending change and the original receipt. She called the ground agent. The ground agent boarded with a scanner and a look like she had already had this morning. "14A is this passenger," she said, pointing at me. Quarter-zip stood. His wife stayed in 14B. They did not get the lounge. I sat down. The mint gum smell faded. At baggage claim the airline chat offered five thousand miles. I took them. I did not write a novel. I attached the same three screenshots to the survey. The survey asked if I felt cared for. I wrote: I felt seated. I wore the same coat to the funeral. 14A had a scuff from his bag. I left it.

social.video_title: Ground crew walked on and pointed at my receipt — Part 2/2
social.description: The pending change died in the aisle. Miles showed up later. Was anxiety ever a boarding pass?
